categories.name: Child Development
categories.description: What actually changes between two and sixteen, why two children the same age can look nothing alike, and what is worth watching for.

categories.name: Focus & Behaviour
categories.description: Concentration, attention span, self-control and the transitions that go wrong. What is developing underneath the behaviour you can see.

categories.name: Learning
categories.description: How reading, handwriting and number sense actually arrive, and how to help without turning the kitchen table into a classroom.

categories.name: STEAM
categories.description: Scientific thinking, building, problem solving and the kind of curiosity that survives being tested. Mostly with things you already own.

categories.name: Technology & AI
categories.description: Screens, chatbots, coding and the question underneath all of them: what should a child be able to do that a machine cannot?

categories.name: Communication
categories.description: Vocabulary, listening, speaking up and the quiet child. How expression develops, and why confidence is a by-product rather than a lesson.

categories.name: Emotions & Friends
categories.description: Anger, tantrums, siblings, empathy and belonging. What a child is still building before they can manage any of it on their own.

categories.name: Health & Safety
categories.description: Sleep, movement, sensory needs, body safety and online safety. The ordinary things that quietly decide how the rest of the week goes.

categories.name: Life Skills
categories.description: Chores, money, responsibility and resilience. The practical competence a child leaves home with, built one ordinary task at a time.

categories.name: Bharatiya Wisdom
categories.description: Panchakosha, dharma, seva, Sanskrit and cultural identity: set beside what child development can and cannot claim about them.

categories.name: Gurukul Education
categories.description: How the gurukul actually worked, what it got right about learning, and which of its principles survive contact with a modern childhood.

categories.name: Nature & Creativity
categories.description: Outdoor play, free play, boredom and making things. The unstructured hours that do more developmental work than most timetables.

categories.name: Parenting
categories.description: Listening, boundaries, shouting, guilt and comparison. The part nobody asks about, answered without pretending it is simple.

categories.name: Learning Science
categories.description: What research actually establishes about play, memory, attention and movement, including where the evidence is thinner than the headlines.

categories.name: Global Education
categories.description: Finland, Japan, Singapore, Montessori, Waldorf, NEP 2020 and homeschooling. What each is actually built on, and what travels.
